title: Nightly infra ops log and quick checklist
content:
Night checks (short):

- context: running nights this week while SRE is OOO. primary focus: GPU pool stability, cross-region routing flakiness, and burst autoscale behavior. quick log and TODOs so I don't forget anything.

- immediate healthchecks (run first, then check dashboards):
  1) nvidia-smi on node-gpu-03 / node-gpu-07 — look for stale processes (>12h) and memory fragmentation.
  2) check pod restarts: kubectl get pods -n gpu-serving -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|Error"
  3) check autoscaler events: kubectl describe hpa gpu-serving-autoscaler -n gpu-serving | tail -n 60
  4) netlink errors on edge-router-{a,b}: sudo dmesg | grep -i "NETDEV|link" -- if present, escalate to network team.

- Recent incidents to note:
  * 2026-03-12 22:10 UTC — brief spike in queue length for hosted-api/us-west-2 that pushed requests to dedicated fallback; saw ~30% higher latency. likely cause: misplaced autoscaler window + a rollout to model-encoder-v2 (quantized) increased memory pressure.
  * I checked logs: encoder-v2 pods had elevated OOM-kills (oom_score_adj?). opening follow-up ticket if repeats.

- Night TODO (priority order):
  [ ] drain node-gpu-03 and run full nv-persist reset (follow runbook steps) — ticket INFRA-4721 related
  [ ] add temporary alert for L2 cache thrash (cheap metric) on serving runtime (threshold: 95th p99 > 12s cpu spin)
  [ ] patch edge-router BGP flaps: add route dampening candidate (need sign-off from netops)
  [ ] verify KV cache util on large-context models — run small script to measure hit-rate per model (script: misc/kv_cache_check.sh)
  [ ] confirm dedicated pool burst config: max-burst=3 -> should hold during regen jobs; if not, raise to 4 for 4h maintenance window

- Quick commands I ran / notes:
  * nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY | grep -A3 "Used"  # node-gpu-03: saw 220MB fragmentation - okay for now
  * kubectl logs gpu-serving-encoder-7 -n gpu-serving | grep "kv_cache_miss" | head -n 40  # some miss storms around 22:05
  * checked autoscaler events: saw scale-down cooldown triggered at 21:58 despite queue rising at 22:00 -> investigate cooldown window logic (maybe using observedMetric vs request count)

- Observations / hypotheses:
  * encoder-v2 quantization path might increase peak working set occasionally, LRU eviction in runtime not aggressive enough -> manifests as OOM/pss spikes
  * routing fallback during capacity blips points to policy order: prefer latency-tier > cost-tier. maybe flip policy to prefer same-region fallback first to reduce cross-region jitter.

- Followups (when not on-call):
  - pair with @Priya to rewrite autoscaler metric to be token-rate-weighted instead of raw qlen (INFRA-4748).
  - bake a small e2e test in CI that runs synthetic load on encoder variants for 1k tokens to catch cache thrash regressions (approx script: tests/load/encoder-smoke.sh).
  - propose change to rollout policy: allow 10% canary on dedicated-pool when model memory delta > 1.5GB.

- Notes to self (personal reminders):
  * document how to safely bump dedicated burst for <4h maintenance without breaking billing alerts — ask finance for a quick approval email template.
  * remember to record times in incident timeline in INFRA-4721. small timestamps matter for correlation with infra-metrics.

- End of shift checklist before handoff:
  [ ] confirm node drains completed / nodes uncordoned if no issues
  [ ] leave summary message in #oncall-handoffs with brief bullet points + links
  [ ] update INFRA-4721 with commands run + upload nv-smi dumps (s3://redwood-infra-dumps/2026-03-13/)

-- quick brain-dump of potential optimizations for later:
  - experiment: reduce default kv_cache TTL for quantized-models by 30% to reduce memory pressure during heavy load bursts.
  - add short-term metric: pod_kv_cache_utilization_ratio (serve runtime exports). create Grafana panel.
  - consider hinting mechanism at routing layer: if model-version annotated "high-ram-variant", avoid sending to smallest dedicated nodes.

(rough/will tidy later)
notes: personal night-shift scratchpad; not a runbook. keep ephemeral. will convert top items to tickets if repeated.
